PullRequest.Title: chat: let language model providers contribute an icon for the model picker
PullRequest.Body:

Refs #339167

Lets a language model provider declare an icon for itself, so its tab in the tabbed model picker shows its brand instead of the generic sparkle. Copilot's OpenRouter provider uses this with OpenRouter's logo.

## What changed

- **Contribution point:** `languageModelChatProviders` entries accept an `icon`, like `languageModelTools` and `chatSessions` do:
  - `"$(name)"` for a codicon, or a glyph contributed through `contributes.icons`
  - `"path/to/icon.svg"` for one image in every theme
  - `{ "light": …, "dark": … }` for separate images per theme

  Paths resolve against the extension folder. A malformed value, or a path that leaves the extension folder, is dropped with a warning in the extension's log.
- **Model picker tabs:** a provider's tab, and its empty "sign in" state, show the declared icon. Providers without one keep today's name matching.
- **Tab strip (`TabbedActionListWidget`):** tabs can show image icons. Light and dark images are switched by theme class. Inactive image tabs are drawn at 70% opacity to match the muted codicons (`descriptionForeground` is the foreground at 70%), and hovering brightens them in the model picker. A tab showing only an image also gets the text-button styling it would otherwise miss, because `Button` never applies it for an empty label.
- **OpenRouter:** Copilot's `openrouter` provider declares OpenRouter's official glyphs from https://openrouter.ai/brand, unmodified: Ink for light themes and Cloud for dark themes. We have permission from OpenRouter to use them.

## Notes for reviewers

- I left groups that a trusted source presentation renames (e.g. "ChatGPT") on name matching, because the vendor's icon wouldn't match the name shown.
- Per-model icons are in the follow-up PR, which is stacked on this one.

## How to test

1. Add an OpenRouter API key through **Chat: Manage Language Models**.
2. Open the chat model picker. The OpenRouter tab shows the OpenRouter logo: dimmed when inactive, full strength when hovered or selected.
3. Switch between light, dark and high contrast themes. The logo switches between its black and white versions.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/tabbedActionListWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerTabs.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/languageModels.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerTabbedWidget.test.ts`: **266 passing**
- After the extension-folder path check was added: `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/languageModels.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerTabs.test.ts`: **113 passing**
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: passed
- Hygiene (pre-commit hook): passed
- Checked in the component explorer with a temporary fixture (not committed): dark, light and high contrast dark themes, plus active, inactive and hover states.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added helper, per-model call sites, and repeated destination-build path are explicit. The PR's test covers an agent-host provider group absent from the configured group map, proving fallback reachability; only real-world catalogue size is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: vendor-array allocations, context-expression parsing/evaluation, and linear scans
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(R*M*V), for fallback models M, visible vendors V, and destination rebuild count R; a picker show rebuilds destinations at least twice.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased UI-path latency and CPU/GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Fallback grouping scanned visible vendors for the display name but did not perform a second vendor snapshot and scan to obtain an icon.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Provider icon resolution now rebuilds and scans the visible-vendor collection once for every fallback-group model.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new helper's added return at RIGHT line 798 creates and scans `languageModelsService.getVendors()` on every icon lookup, and the diff calls this helper from `getProviderGroupForModel`, which runs inside the `userModels` loop.
Findings.Title: Reuse one vendor snapshot for provider icons
Findings.Impact: With a large relayed-provider catalogue, opening or rebuilding the model picker performs avoidable CPU work and short-lived allocations, increasing popup latency and GC pressure.
Findings.Evidence: `getLanguageModelProviderIcon` calls `getVendors().find`. The concrete service implementation of `getVendors()` allocates `Array.from(_vendors.values())`, filters every vendor, deserializes each `when` expression, and evaluates context keys. `buildModelPickerDestinations` invokes the helper through `getProviderGroupForModel` for each fallback user model, while `_showCurrent` builds destinations before showing and again from `createActionList` (plus an optional sizing build).
Findings.Recommendation: Snapshot visible vendors once per destination build and pass a vendor descriptor/icon map into grouping, or resolve display name and icon together from one descriptor lookup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Register or remove language-model provider extension contributions during startup or extension changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Runs while language-model provider contributions are registered. Icon validation and URI joining must complete before descriptors are published, but perform only bounded in-memory work per contributed provider.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of added or removed language-model provider contributions, with constant work per icon path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The extension-point handler processes added and removed contributions synchronously and serially; no new task, queue, limiter, or concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No runtime cache is involved. Contribution values are processed once per extension-point add event; resolved URI and ThemeIcon objects are retained in the vendor descriptor. Removal discards the descriptor through the existing vendor lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed handler performs regex checks, URI joining, containment checks, shallow copies, and map updates only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of provider contributions varies, but is realistically small and each icon has at most two paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new parsing is bounded per provider, adds no filesystem/network call, and retains only one small icon descriptor per vendor.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, search, refresh, or switch tabs in the model picker with user-provided or agent-host-relayed models
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Destination grouping and tab DOM construction run synchronously before the picker is usable. The current-theme image fetch/decode affects icon paint but is asynchronous and does not gate list construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The browser resolves, loads, parses, and paints the contributed SVG through a CSS background image.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: On a cold cache, at most one current-theme image request per distinct image-backed provider URI; repeated tab and welcome uses share the same URI and browser cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider tabs and welcome states used bundled codicon CSS and did not load provider-contributed image resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request affects icon paint only; picker list construction and interaction do not await it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fallback-group model count after grouping-map misses, multiplied by visible vendor count and destination rebuild count; icon I/O scales only with distinct image provider URIs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model grouping is serial on the UI thread. `_showCurrent` rebuilds destinations before showing and `createActionList` rebuilds them again, with a possible sizing build. Browser icon requests may run concurrently and are bounded by image-backed provider count.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider descriptors are held in the service, but `getVendors()` does not cache its filtered result: every call allocates a new array and re-evaluates vendor `when` clauses. Browser image resources are keyed by resolved URI; a cold picker loads the current-theme asset once per image-backed provider and subsequent renders use the browser cache/coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new icon fallback invokes `getVendors()` in the per-model grouping loop, and the concrete implementation allocates, filters, parses `when` clauses, and evaluates context keys on every invocation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Relayed catalogues can range from a few models to a provider's full catalogue, so exact added latency is uncertain; the O(R*M*V) repeated vendor enumeration is nevertheless established.
Scenarios.Verdict: One low-severity repeated-work regression was reported for the added per-model vendor snapshot/scan. Image loading itself is bounded, cacheable, and off the picker-construction critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch between light, dark, and high-contrast themes while the model picker is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Theme-class changes synchronously update style and paint selection. A first switch to the other variant can initiate one asynchronous resource load per distinct image URI but does not block theme state propagation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: CSS selects and the browser loads the dark or light SVG background resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one additional cold load for the alternate-theme URI per distinct image-backed provider; warm switches issue no new resource transfer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Codicon-based provider icons changed color through existing theme CSS and required no alternate provider asset.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: May delay only the alternate icon's paint; it does not block the picker or theme switch logic.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and complexity of distinct image-backed provider icons visible during a theme switch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The browser may fetch newly selected theme assets concurrently. Aggregate concurrency is bounded by the number of visible image-backed provider icons; no loop launches subprocess, IPC, database, or service calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Light and dark assets have distinct URI cache keys. Only the CSS-selected theme asset is referenced for painting; after each variant has been loaded once, browser caching serves later theme switches. There is no unbounded application cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for selection and cache cardinality; exact decode cost depends on extension-provided image complexity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Third-party extensions may contribute larger images than the bundled OpenRouter SVGs, but request count remains bounded by visible providers and normal browser resource caching.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The work is required by the feature, bounded by provider count, browser-cached, and not awaited on an interaction critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and dispose a generic tabbed action-list popup containing image-backed tabs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Creating a generic `TabbedActionListWidget` popup synchronously adds one pseudo-element configuration and two CSS custom-property writes for each image-backed tab before interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attach CSS background-image URLs that cause browser resource loading for image-backed tabs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active-theme resource load per distinct cold image URI, regardless of repeated tabs using that URI; zero transfer on warm cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The widget accepted ThemeIcon values only and rendered codicon text without loading tab image assets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asset paint is asynchronous; two style-property writes and class additions per image tab are synchronous but bounded by tab count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of image-backed tabs in one popup, not number of list rows or models.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM construction is serial on the UI thread. Resource loads are browser-managed and bounded by distinct active-theme image URIs; no changed IPC, subprocess, database, or explicit network loop exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is added. CSS URL strings and pseudo-elements live only for the popup DOM lifetime; disposing the popup releases those elements and inline style references. Browser resource caching follows normal URI caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed loop performs constant DOM/style work per tab and popup disposal already owns the created DOM.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Other widget consumers may eventually supply more or more-complex image tabs, but tab strips are small UI collections rather than unbounded model rows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Synchronous work is O(tab count), retained state follows the existing popup lifecycle, and boundary calls are cacheable and bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 14 changed files and all diff pages. Traced provider contribution registration, destination grouping/rebuilds, tab and welcome rendering, theme changes, browser asset loads, caching, concurrency, and popup cleanup. Submitted one low-severity repeated-work finding for per-model vendor re-enumeration; no other concrete performance regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
